facts.statement: The genus Paraorthacodus was described by Glückman in 1957.
Paraorthacodus belongs to the family Paraorthacodontidae, which is classified within either the order Hexanchiformes or Synechodontiformes.
facts.quote: It a member of the family Paraorthacodontidae (though it was formerly regarded as a member of the family Palaeospinacidae), which is either placed in Hexanchiformes or in Synechodontiformes.

facts.statement: The genus spans from the Early Jurassic to the Paleocene, or possibly the Eocene.
facts.quote: It is known from over a dozen named species spanning from the Early Jurassic to the Paleocene, or possibly Eocene.

facts.statement: Most species of Paraorthacodus are known only from isolated teeth.
facts.quote: Almost all members of the genus are exclusively known from isolated teeth

facts.statement: The teeth featured a single large central cusp with shorter lateral cusplets designed for clutching prey.
facts.quote: The dentition had teeth with a single large central cusp along with shorter lateral cusplets, which were designed for clutching.

facts.statement: Paraorthacodus teeth differ from Synechodus because their lateral cusplets decrease in size linearly rather than exponentially.
facts.quote: The teeth are distinguished from those of Synechodus by the lateral cusplets decreasing in size linearly away from the central cusp rather than exponentially as in Synechodus.

facts.statement: The species possessed a single dorsal fin located towards the rear of the body without a fin spine.
facts.quote: There was only a single dorsal fin towards the back of the body without a fin spine.

facts.statement: Fossils of P. jurensis from Late Jurassic Germany suggest juveniles had robust bodies with round heads, while adults had large fusiform profiles.
facts.quote: P. jurensis from the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous of Europe, which is known from full body fossils from the Late Jurassic of Germany, which suggest that juveniles had a robust body with a round head, while adults had large body sizes with a fusiform profile.

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Hettangian to the Priabonian, approximately 201.4 to 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Priabonian (201.4 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Paraorthacodus is the family Palaeospinacidae.
Paraorthacodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
